title: Davis Schneider becomes free agent after 4 seasons with Blue Jays | CBC Sports
html:
MLB·Updated

Davis Schneider becomes free agent after 4 seasons with Blue Jays

Club offered contracts to every other unsigned player on 40-man roster

Davis Schneider became a free agent Friday after the Toronto Blue Jays declined to offer him a contract for 2027.

The club offered contracts to all seven of its other arbitration-eligible players, including infielder Ernie Clement, outfielder Nathan Lukes and reliever Louis Varland.

The 27-year-old infielder and outfielder split the 2026 season between Toronto and Triple-A Buffalo. He hit .145 with five home runs and 16 RBIs in 69 games with the Blue Jays.

He batted .206 with 37 homers and 113 RBIs in 321 games over four seasons with Toronto.

Fan favourite

The mustachioed Schneider made a historic entrance to the majors in August 2023 and quickly became a fan favourite in Toronto.

He homered in his first at-bat at Fenway Park and became the first player in major-league history to collect nine hits, including two home runs, in his first three games.

His biggest moment as a Jay came in Game 5 of the 2025 World Series, when he filled in for injured leadoff hitter George Springer and homered on the first pitch from Dodgers left-hander Blake Snell.

The Blue Jays won 6-1 at Dodger Stadium to take a 3-2 series lead, but the L.A. won the next two games in Toronto to claim the title.

Jays trade Lee

The Blue Jays also traded right-handed reliever Chase Lee to the Colorado Rockies for cash Friday.

Lee posted a 6.52 earned-run average in eight appearances for Toronto this season, striking out five and walking eight in 9 2/3 innings.

Toronto designated Lee for assignment Thursday after claiming infielder Christian Cairo off waivers from the Los Angeles Dodgers.
summary: Davis Schneider became a free agent Friday after the Toronto Blue Jays declined to offer him a contract for 2027.
